long_biography.plain_text:
Richland Rum turned a childhood fascination into Erik Vonk’s most personal operating business. His Dutch grandfather taught him the difference between molasses-based rum and spirits made directly from sugarcane. Decades later, Vonk and his wife Karin planted cane on their Georgia farm and developed a single-estate distillery built around control from field to bottle.

The Vonks moved production into downtown Richland, restoring buildings for distilling, ageing and hospitality before adding a coastal site in Brunswick. The company grows its feedstock, makes syrup, distils in copper pots and matures the spirit on site. That integrated model has made the distillery both a drinks producer and a contributor to rural tourism and local economic activity.
